_doc: Point-in-time retrospective. Every input was public on as_of; see sources. Hindsight lives only in outcome.json.
methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); net premiums earned, combined ratio, investment income, book value and pre-tax margin signals with ACE's rule-T thresholds

pit_profile.why: 'are a global insurance and reinsurance organization, serving the needs of a diverse group of clients worldwide' 'Insurance and reinsurance markets are historically cyclical, and we expect to experience periods with excess underwriting capacity and unfavorable premium rates.' 'The incidence and severity of catastrophes are inherently unpredictable and our losses from catastrophes could be substantial.' (FY2013 10-K, Items 1 and 1A): the company calls its own business cyclical (the XOM, CAT and GOOG reading), so CYCLICAL; catastrophe losses are the business's own recurring cost, not a substitution theme; no disruption theme in taxonomy_eras.json is live for a property and casualty insurer on this date (of the live themes, OFFSHORE is scoped to 'lower-cost offshore delivery (Indian IT services) takes share and price from Western consulting, systems integration and outsourcing', CLOUD to 'public cloud displaces on-premise hardware, storage, legacy databases and data-center outsourcing', ECOMMERCE to 'e-commerce (Amazon effect) displaces physical retail, malls, grocery, distribution': none names insurance), so the watch list is empty and these words stay here (the PEP obesity rule)

classification.quality_note: 'are a global insurance and reinsurance organization, serving the needs of a diverse group of clients worldwide' 'Insurance and reinsurance markets are historically cyclical, and we expect to experience periods with excess underwriting capacity and unfavorable premium rates.' (FY2013 10-K, Items 1 and 1A): the company calls its own business cyclical (the XOM, CAT and GOOG reading), so CYCLICAL; catastrophe losses are the business's own recurring cost, not a substitution theme; no disruption theme in taxonomy_eras.json is live for a property and casualty insurer on this date (of the live themes, OFFSHORE is scoped to 'lower-cost offshore delivery (Indian IT services) takes share and price from Western consulting, systems integration and outsourcing', CLOUD to 'public cloud displaces on-premise hardware, storage, legacy databases and data-center outsourcing', ECOMMERCE to 'e-commerce (Amazon effect) displaces physical retail, malls, grocery, distribution': none names insurance), so the watch list is empty and these words stay here (the PEP obesity rule). cyclical (obsolescence risk 2/5); price rich; Ratio B 1.42x; +31% to EPP floor; model-vs-market gap -0.47; conservative 2yr -19%.

BEAR.desc: EPS -54.7%/yr (worst year FY04-FY13, capped at 0%); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS -1.6%/yr (Q3 revenue YoY + margin + buyback); P/E at its 10-yr median

BULL.desc: EPS +12.2%/yr (FY04-FY13 CAGR, at least BASE); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +61.6%/yr (best 2-yr run FY04-FY13, at least BULL); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: ACE (retrospective, 2015-01-02) ◐ WATCHLIST — Ratio B 1.42x (88.2% downside to Bear $13.50 / +62.1% upside to Bull $185.49) | Adj composite 1.95 vs market 2.41: gap -0.47 [MODESTLY OVERVALUED] | +31% above the EPP floor $87.36 (8x FY14E $10.92) | Conservative 2-yr case: -19.0% total (-9.5%/yr) | At 10.5x FY14E the 15% hurdle price $151.35 sits between the BASE and BULL cases; revenue +0.5% YoY in Q3 2014, forward revenues +0.5% (Q3 2014 revenue growth (no Q4 2014 guide)); no disruption theme has dated evidence.
